shots.action: A miner's dusty hands wind a band round a note on the drill pipe, just above the bit; his face is behind it in a lamp's beam, squinting. Grit falls. The pipe jerks and starts to rise; he lets go and looks up, eyes wide
shots.camera: Close at eye level, pushing in

shots.action: The pipe goes back up into the roof with the note on it. Three miners under it throw their arms up and shout after it; stones rattle down
The surface, night: the bit clears the hole in a puff of dust, the note tied on above it. A rescuer bends and reaches for it, mouth open. Rook, on the deck, leans over with his arms folded
shots.camera: Low, moving in on the bit

shots.action: Rook on the deck beside the hanging bit: he unfolds one arm and jabs a wing at the note, eyes half shut. The rescuer still has both hands out to it
Close: he leans in to the note, hat brim down, and taps his beak
shots.camera: Close on his face and the note

shots.action: A rescuer unfolds the note in both hands under a floodlight, reads, and his mouth falls open. Rook reads over his shoulder, hand at his chin; his hat jumps
A card: the creased note held to the light, the words written out in red, line by line: WE ARE FINE / IN THE SHELTER, / THE 33 OF US
Seventeen days earlier, an ordinary shift: a pickup rolls down the access road with its lamps on, two miners walking beside it, calm. Rook rides in the back with his arms folded, looking about him
A card: Rook's case file on a steel plate. 5 AUGUST 2010 / SAN JOSÉ MINE / ATACAMA DESERT, CHILE / COPPER AND GOLD, typed in line by line
From further down the road: the two miners walk towards us and past, the truck behind them with its lamps on, Rook in the back turning his head from wall to wall
shots.camera: Low, standing in the road as the truck comes up and passes

shots.action: The lamps along the wall stutter. Rock comes off the roof and a wall of dust rolls down the tunnel; three men spin round and run for the camera beside the truck, mouths open
shots.camera: Low in the tunnel, the dust coming at us

shots.action: The road out: one block of grey rock from wall to wall and floor to roof. Three helmet lamps move over it. Rook raps on it, puts the side of his head to it, hears nothing, and his head goes down
shots.camera: Low, looking up the face of the block

shots.action: Dust so thick the lamps are only glows. Three men feel their way with their arms out, eyes screwed up; Rook coughs with a wing over his beak
shots.camera: Eye level, drifting through the dust

shots.action: A ventilation shaft with a ladder up its wall. One miner climbs hand over hand; two below shine their lamps up after him, one pointing
A card: a cross-section. The road winds down to the shelter and is cut by a red block; beside it the shaft climbs towards the surface, and its ladder stops part-way
Part-way up, the ladder simply stops. He reaches for a rung that is not there, and his head drops. On the ledge beside him Rook looks up the bare wall, then at us, brim down
A card: the same cross-section. A measure runs down from the desert to one small lit room: 700 M
The shelter: men on a bench and on the floor under one lamp, knees up, heads down; the gallery black around them
The food locker: three tins and a carton on bare shelves. A miner in a white helmet reaches in, takes one tin and looks down at it
The foreman stands in front of the men and puts it to them; hands go up along the bench, one after another. At the end of the row Rook looks about him and raises a wing too
shots.camera: Over the room from the gallery side

shots.action: Close: a spoon dips into the open tin, lifts one small heap of tuna and tips it into a cup
A queue of miners with small cups shuffles one step forward. Rook is last in it: he looks into his cup, then slowly at us, brim down
A card: a calendar of days. A spoon on one, a dash on the next, a spoon, a dash
By the water drum: one man fills a cup and drinks, pulling a face; another sits against the wall and drags a forearm across his brow. Rook pants with his beak open and wipes his own
A pickup stands in the gallery with its bonnet up and its lamps burning. A miner holds his helmet lamp to a cable from the battery. Rook touches the other terminal: a spark, and his hat jumps
shots.camera: Low, front quarter of the truck

shots.action: Along the bench: tired faces under helmet lamps, eyes half closed. Rook sits on the floor at the end of the row, hugging his knees, and turns to look along it
The camp at the mine gate at night: three people by a line of small lamps, hands clasped, looking towards the rig. Rook stands apart and flips a coin, waiting
Close: three faces over three candles, heads bowed, the tents behind. Rook stands a little apart with his head down and his brim low; no joke here
The derrick in the floodlights, the pipe turning down into the desert; two rescuers watch the hole
shots.camera: Wide and low, from the other side

shots.action: A card: the cross-section. Seven drill lines go down past the room, one after another, each ending in a red cross

The gallery. Four men stand with their faces turned up as grit trickles from the roof in a line that travels across and away; Rook has the side of his head to the wall. The trickle stops; the heads go down
A drill bit comes down through the gallery roof in a shower of grit. Men run to it, arms up, shouting up the hole; one beats on the steel with a hammer, sparks flying
The same hands, from the other side: the band goes round the paper, the red writing towards us, his face tight with care
From above the men: the pipe slides up past us into the roof with the note on it, three faces turned up after it
shots.camera: High, looking down past the pipe

shots.action: The note open in the rescuer's hands, seen from his other side; Rook's hat is off his head, his beak open
The men at the rig jump with their arms in the air. Rook's hat leaves his head, his beak hangs open and a feather comes loose
Daylight at the borehole, a thin cable running into it. Rook kneels, lays his orange rule across the hole, bends to read it, then sits back and shrugs at us
A card: two circles to the same scale. A small one, THE BOREHOLE; beside it the outline of a man's shoulders, far wider
A second, bigger rig: a wide pipe turns under a winch tower, dust boiling off the collar. Rook, in front with his arms folded, turns his head to us
Daylight at the narrow borehole: two rescuers lower a long thin tube into it on a cable, hand over hand. Rook, on one knee at the collar, bends to watch it go down
Below: the tube comes down out of the roof on its cable. Two miners reach up and take it; one pulls out a bottle and holds it up, grinning, and the others close in
On the bench: a miner reads a sheet of paper in both hands and wipes an eye with his wrist. The men either side lean in. One holds up a small camera; another waves into it
Daylight: three drilling rigs across the hillside, each in its own dust. In front, Rook looks from one to the next to the next, then shrugs at us
shots.hud: PLAN A. PLAN B. PLAN C.

shots.action: A card: the cross-section. Three lines, A, B and C, creep down from three rigs towards the room at different speeds
Under the new shaft, rock rattles down onto a heap. Three miners shovel it into a barrow. Rook has a shovel too, until a stone bounces off his hat; he looks at us
The big rig from the other side, the pipe still turning, dust streaming off it
Below: the wide drill head comes through the gallery roof in a fall of rock. Four miners shield their faces, then throw their arms up
A card: a long thin shaft drawn down through the rock to the room, 620 M and more; beside it a bicycle wheel the width of the shaft

Daylight: the capsule lies on two trestles. One rescuer tightens something at its head, sparks at his hands; another kneels at its side. Rook holds his orange rule across the end of it, reads it, and looks at us
Night at the winch tower: the capsule, banded white, blue and red, hangs on its cable over the shaft, then sinks into it; two rescuers guide it
Rook tries a capsule for size: wedged in the cage, wings pinned, hat squashed crooked, he wriggles and a feather pops out. A rescuer grins
Night at the shaft. A rescuer stands in the cage, raises one hand to the men clapping round him, and the capsule sinks out of the floodlights. Rook touches his brim to him
Below: the capsule comes down out of the roof on its cable and lands in the rubble. Miners watch it all the way down; Rook holds his hat
The rescuer steps out of the cage. The miners close round him; one takes him by both shoulders, the others have their arms in the air. Rook lifts his hat
shots.camera: From the shelter side, moving in

shots.action: One miner stands in the cage. A rescuer checks him and raises a thumb; the miner lifts a hand and the capsule starts up
Cut-away of the shaft: the capsule climbs, rock sliding down past it, sparks at the guide wheels, the cable taut above
shots.camera: Beside the capsule, rising with it, tilted

shots.action: Close through the bars: his face turned up, eyes narrowing as the light from above grows on it
The capsule rises out of the collar under the floodlights. Arms go up all round; Rook flaps into the air
Close: the first man up, in dark glasses against the floodlights. He turns his face up to the night sky, breathes out, and his fists go up
He steps away from the cage with his arms up; a woman runs to him and they hold on. Rescuers clap. Rook's hat goes up
The second man up has a sack. He presses a lump of rock into a rescuer's hands, then one into Rook's. Rook holds it up to the floodlight: it glitters, and his eyes go wide
From the other end of the gallery: the capsule comes down again for the next man, the others waiting under it
The shaft from below the capsule: it climbs away from us up the bore towards a point of light
A card: thirty-three helmets, ticked off one after another. 33 OF 33. 69 DAYS
The gallery, nearly empty. The foreman in his white helmet looks back at the shelter, walks to the capsule, stands in, and it lifts
shots.camera: Wide from the far end of the gallery

shots.action: A card: one line of 69 days. 5 AUGUST, the collapse. 22 AUGUST, the note. 9 OCTOBER, the shaft. 13 OCTOBER, out
The gallery from the shelter end: cups left on the table, the bench bare. Far down the tunnel the capsule rises into the roof with the last rescuer in it, and the lamps go down behind him
Day. The rigs and the tower are gone; a steel lid is bolted over the shaft, dust blowing across it. Rook stands over it with his brim down, then looks up at the hills
Rook's case board, a scuffed steel plate: a photograph of the capsule at the surface. 33 OF 33. 69 DAYS. Stamped TRUE
Dawn at the site, the capsule standing by the tower. Rook turns to us and shrugs
He picks a steel drill tooth out of the dust, turns it in the light, pockets it and pulls his hat brim down
